attendance: Present: President Jennifer Munro, Vice President Michael Shaughnessy, Brian McCambridge, Victor Chau, Anna Turcotte, Amy Faulkingham, Gary Rairdon. Mayor David Morse also attended.

blocks.x: Mayor’s Message: Suboxone Administration & Recovery Support Initiative
EMS Opioid-Overdose Pilot Program (MOUD Initiative)
Discussion Summary

Mayor Morse opened with a Memorial Day reminder: the parade and Riverbank Park ceremony are Monday, May 25. Morse then introduced Fire Chief Stephen Sloan. Sloan presented a new emergency medical services (EMS) pilot program in which buprenorphine (Suboxone) is given in the field following an overdose. It is called the “MOUD” (Medication for Opioid Use Disorder) initiative.

Chief Sloan reported that Westbrook is currently the only fire department in Maine approved for this pilot. Five other agencies may enroll later: United Ambulance, Redington-Fairview Hospital, Portland, Biddeford Fire, and Waterville Fire. Westbrook would be the lead/data site over the pilot's 36-month run.
2025 Westbrook data:
59 overdoses (just under 3% of the statewide total).
24 patients were transported and 35 refused care.
Naloxone (a drug that reverses overdoses) was administered to 17 who then refused further care.
Police responded to four additional overdoses that didn't require EMS.

Sloan also reported 22 fatal overdoses recorded through EMS run report data, two of them in Westbrook. Maine is near the worst in the nation for overdose rate per 100,000 residents; only West Virginia is worse. Without intervention, Sloan projected the City could lose roughly 6–10 residents to overdose over the pilot's 3-year span.
Program goals: 15% of contacted overdose patients engaged in a treatment program, 55–65% linked to definitive care, and an adverse-event rate under 2%.
Follow-up protocol:
A fire department team member contacts the patient within 24 hours.
The police department's recovery liaison follows up within 48 hours.
The patient is linked to Maine Health's Comprehensive Addiction Medicine Center within 72 hours.
Cost: already budgeted, roughly $1,000/year for medication.
Several councilors expressed strong support. President Munro cited friends and family affected by overdose loss. Councilor Faulkingham, who works in the field, asked to see the pilot's results.

Councilor Chau asked about liability for administering the wrong drug. Sloan said the greater liability risk is actually in allowing a patient to refuse care untreated, and that buprenorphine is a low-risk medication.
City Clerk Ledoux then gave a brief absentee-voting update ahead of the June 9 state primary/school budget referendum.
Key Decisions
Informational — no vote taken.

None.

Resolve 2026-13 — Overnight Spring Street Closure for Water Utility Work
Found on page 37 of the packet.
Discussion Summary
Authorizes an overnight closure of Spring Street (Thomas Drive to the South Portland municipal boundary), 7 PM–7 AM, for a water-main connection to a residential project at 984 Spring Street.
Representatives from Procopio Companies (developer) and Sargent Corporation (contractor) explained a three-day plan:
First is a daytime single-lane closure to prepare the site (Tuesday, May 26).
Next is the full overnight closure for excavation and tie-in (Wednesday, May 27).
Last is a final daytime single-lane closure to repave (Thursday, May 28).
The work goes ahead rain or shine.

Councilor Rairdon asked whether the officer should be at the County Road traffic light rather than Thomas Drive, to keep cars from driving about 200 yards first. Assistant City Administrator Franceschi relayed that Police Captain Goldberg had determined that the Spiller Drive/Thomas Drive staging was actually safer.
It keeps officers out of the signalized intersection, given low overnight traffic volume.
Key Decisions
Passed by unanimous roll call, 7–0. Moved by Gary Rairdon, seconded by Victor Chau.
Action Items
None.

Order 2026-61 — Davan Indoor Pool — Emergency Motor Repair Confirmation
Found on page 57 of the packet.
Discussion Summary

Confirms, after the fact, an $8,348.30 expenditure to Christman Pool Service for a replacement motor at the Davan Indoor Pool (Westbrook Community Center). The Mayor made the expenditure under emergency authority. Director Greg Post's team caught early signs of corrosion and leaks in the 12-year-old motor before it failed. The City's last full motor failure, in 2014, flooded the Community Center basement with five feet of standing water.
Key Decisions
Passed by unanimous roll call, 7–0 (first reading). Moved by Gary Rairdon, seconded by Victor Chau.

It also authorizes a $6,850 purchase of five 100' large-diameter supply hoses from Harrison Shrader Enterprises. Order 2026-63 — Pyxis Medication-Storage Rental Agreement
Found on page 68 of the packet.
Discussion Summary
Authorizes a five-year, $11,172/year rental agreement with CareFusion Solutions for a BD Pyxis MedStation and supply tower. It is funded from opioid settlement funds.

This responds to a 2017 Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) rule that is now being enforced. As of July 14, 2026, hospitals will no longer supply the Fire Department's controlled medications (fentanyl, Versed/midazolam, ketamine). The Department must obtain its own DEA license and securely store and dispense them in-house.
Council Q&A covered security:
A biometric scan plus a unique passcode.
Dual-provider verification required to dispense.
A daily tamper-seal check at shift change.
Only three chiefs authorized to restock.
A 3-vial-per-call dispensing cap.

Council Q&A also covered the rent-vs-buy rationale. The ~60-day compliance deadline favored renting now, with a possible switch to outright purchase in a future year once the Department's auditing processes are proven out.
On June 1, City Administrator Holmes told the Council the vendor had since said a mid-agreement switch would extend the rental agreement.
Key Decisions
Passed by unanimous roll call, 7–0 (first reading). Moved by Brian McCambridge, seconded by Victor Chau.
Action Items
None.
Order 2026-64 — Westbrook Trail Blazes — Trail Grooming Equipment Funding
Found on page 82 of the packet.
Discussion Summary

Authorizes a $30,000 Recreation & Conservation Commission expenditure to the Westbrook Trail Blazes snowmobile club for trail-grooming equipment (a Polaris Ranger and track system, retail value over $40,000). Club president Dan McCarthy described the club's 18-year partnership with the City. He also described 30+ miles of multi-use trails (also used by hikers, bikers, and cross-country skiers) and roughly 1,000 volunteer hours this year alone. Councilors Rairdon and Chau both praised the club at length.
Key Decisions
Passed by unanimous roll call, 7–0 (first reading). Moved by Gary Rairdon, seconded by Victor Chau. Second and final reading is scheduled for the June 1, 2026 meeting.

None.
Second Public Comment
Blood Drive Announcement & E-Bike Nighttime Glare Safety Concern
Discussion Summary

Dennis Marrotte, a member of the Stephen Manchester American Legion Post, announced an upcoming Red Cross blood drive (Friday, June 12, 9 AM–2 PM, at the Post next to Riverbank Park). He also announced a second drive planned for October 9.

Speaking separately as a member of the Westbrook Safe Mobility Access Committee, he raised a nighttime safety concern about e-bikes and electric scooters with bright headlights blinding oncoming drivers. He described a recent incident at the Forest Street/Main Street intersection, where his windshield was briefly whited out by oncoming e-bike headlights.
Key Decisions
Informational — no vote taken.

None.
